evidence.text: Concern:  The 2024 BMW 530i is equipped with "Dynamic Cruise Control" and a "Speed Limit Assistant." The system is designed to automatically adopt posted speed limits and adjust the cruise control set speed. However, because this specific trim lacks a radar-based distance-monitoring sensor (Active Cruise Control), the vehicle initiates aggressive, unintended acceleration toward slower-moving traffic or stopped obstacles whenever it detects a higher speed limit sign.  Safety Risk: While the vehicle is using its cameras to "see" and adopt an external speed command, it remains "blind" to the actual traffic directly in its path. This creates a high risk of rear-end collisions, as the car will prioritize reaching the new speed limit even if it means accelerating directly into the bumper of a lead vehicle.  Proposed Solution: A "Dynamic" cruise control system that has the authority to control acceleration based on external data MUST also have the authority to maintain a safe following distance. I propose that BMW should be required to include distance-monitoring features in all cruise control systems that utilize automated speed adoption. If the hardware for distance-keeping is not present, the car should not be permitted to automatically increase speed based on roadside signs.  Inspection Status: The vehicle is available for inspection. No warning lamps appeared prior to these incidents, as the system is operating exactly as programmed by the manufacturer, which highlights a fundamental logic and design failure.

The instrument cluster simultaneously displayed: "Vehicle may roll. Brake manually," "Drive carefully. Changed steering effort," "Drive carefully. Chassis stabilization," and "Parking assistance malfunction." Auto Hold and the electronic parking brake's hold function were disabled, requiring manual brake application to prevent rollaway. Mileage at incident: approximately 21,344 miles. The simultaneous failure of Electric Power Steering, Dynamic Stability Control, and the Electronic Parking Brake while the vehicle was in motion in traffic created an immediate safety hazard. No crash or injury occurred, but a recurrence at highway speed, on a wet road, or during an evasive maneuver could foreseeably cause loss of vehicle control, crash, injury, or death. The vehicle was taken to an authorized BMW dealer. The technician stated this failure is a known issue following a recent vehicle software update, that BMW has no repair available, and that the only action taken was to power-cycle the vehicle and clear stored fault codes. No software remedy, parts replacement, or TSB was provided. I was given no assurance the failure will not recur and no timeline for a fix. To my knowledge, no recall has been issued for this defect on the i5 platform. I request that NHTSA evaluate the scope of this issue across the i5 fleet and determine whether a defect investigation or recall is warranted.

While driving in heavy highway traffic at approximately 5–10 mph, the vehicle suddenly displayed a red warning message and symbol in the driver’s gauge cluster indicating the car was shutting down. About 15–20 seconds later, propulsion was completely lost, although power steering and braking remained available.  I attempted to change gears and restart the car by turning it on and off, but nothing worked. I activated the hazard lights since the car was stopped in traffic and posed a danger to surrounding vehicles. Because the vehicle would not respond, I opened and closed the driver’s door and then attempted to restart. At that point, the vehicle restarted, and I was able to continue driving. I was driving a brand-new 2025 BMW i5 electric car, just leased from dealer the day before. The car was at rest, waiting for traffic light to turn green. Then the car started to move forward, and suddenly hit the car in front with a big thrust. My foot was on the brake trying to stop the car, but I felt like being hit by another car behind me, twice, the second time being the final thrust. My wife on the passenger side also felt the car shaking before the collision. Looking back after the collision, there was actually no car hitting mine. I believe the braking system failed. I have downloaded the video recordings from the car, with 30 seconds before and 30 seconds after the accident, by front, rear, left and right cameras, confirming that the car was at rest for about 20 seconds, then moving forward, and finally accelerating with a big thrust into the collision. I wish to have the Event Data Recorder (EDR) data to verify the pressure I applied on the brake pedal (or/and the pressure on the accelerator pedal as others may speculate that I did), to nail down the facts.  Two cars in front of mime were damaged, and one lady driver had injury. Luckily all cars were initially at rest. With higher speed and such brake failure it can cause deaths.  I have reported the problem to the BMW dealer in Rockville, Maryland. I will report to BMW manufacturer too. The dealer said BMW can send engineer to pull the EDR data and investigate. It will take time though.  I have reported the accident to insurance company. I'll talk with the insurance agent assigned to the case next Monday, to discuss what he wants to do for inspection.  In addition to the brake failure, there was no automatic emergency braking, or forward collision warning, as in my previous leased BMW car. The dealer did set up safety features before leasing the car to me, such as the video recording 30 seconds before and after. This makes the accident more surprising.

signals.title: Love how fast and powerful it feels
signals.summary: Customers say the car delivers strong acceleration, great pickup, and a smooth, enjoyable driving feel. Many also appreciate the efficiency and convenience of the electric or plug-in hybrid drivetrain, making everyday driving more satisfying.

signals.title: Smooth and comfortable ride with sporty, responsive handling
signals.summary: Customers say the car rides very smoothly and feels comfortable while still delivering a sporty, nimble driving experience. They praise its quiet, refined nature and how well it responds to driver inputs.

signals.title: Love the car's exterior styling
signals.summary: Customers say they really like the car's exterior look and styling. They praise the color options and sporty yet luxurious appearance, and report getting compliments and attention for the design.

signals.title: Drives like a dream and feels luxurious
signals.summary: Customers say the car is fun to drive, with a smooth ride, strong performance, and responsive handling that makes driving satisfying. Many also mention a comfortable, well‑finished cabin and tech features that add to the overall enjoyment.

signals.title: I really love the interior design
signals.summary: Customers are very pleased with the interior, praising the look, color combinations, materials, and refined layout. Many say it feels luxurious, is easy to keep clean, and is preferable to previous cars they owned.

signals.title: Interior feels very comfortable and luxurious
signals.summary: Customers consistently say the interior is comfortable and gives a luxurious, upscale feel. Many note it is more comfortable than their previous cars or other brands and is well suited for long trips.

signals.title: Seats are very comfortable and supportive
signals.summary: Customers say the seats are very comfortable and supportive, and many like the Veganza and leather materials. They also value the seat automatically moving back when unbuckled, the strong side bolsters during sporty driving, and the leg extension that eases knee pain.

signals.title: Hands free trunk doesn't work consistently
signals.summary: Customers report the touchless kick-to-open trunk often fails or only activates after repeated tries, and sometimes opens randomly or with a lag. They find the required motion too picky and frustrating when their hands are full.

signals.title: Range feels limited and fluctuates
signals.summary: Customers say the real-world electric range is lower than they expected and the range display often jumps around or shows inconsistent estimates. This causes anxiety on longer trips and leads owners to rely on gasoline or public chargers, especially in cold weather or areas with few chargers.

signals.title: Seat height doesn't go high enough
signals.summary: Customers report the driver seat cannot be raised enough to get a clear view over the hood or around the instrument/passenger bar, which is especially problematic for shorter drivers. They also say the seats can be too firm, the bolsters can press uncomfortably or fail to hold smaller occupants, and some seat adjustments are confusing or don't work as expected.

signals.title: Love the large touchscreen and long display
signals.summary: Customers say the new large, long touchscreen looks great and is enjoyable to use, with many praising its design and presence across the dash. Several noted it can feel intimidating at first but quickly proves straightforward and responsive to touch.

signals.title: Power delivery is weak, jerky, or inconsistent
signals.summary: Customers say the car's power delivery doesn't feel right. Some report it feels underpowered and not as peppy as expected, while others experience abrupt surges, jerky launches, delayed engine response when switching power sources, rough idling, and poorer fuel economy than advertised.

signals.title: Size feels just right, not too big or small
signals.summary: Customers appreciate that the car is larger than their previous vehicles but still the right size for everyday use and parking. They say it feels roomy without being too large or hard to handle.

signals.title: Range is better than quoted and fits commute
signals.summary: Customers say the electric/plug‑in range meets or exceeds their expectations for everyday driving and works well with home charging. Many report it reduces gas use, fits their daily commute, and that the displayed range feels accurate and reliable.

signals.title: Brakes squeal, grind, have heavy dust and feel grabby
signals.summary: Customers report loud squeaking or grinding noises, heavy brake dust on the wheels, and braking that feels overly sensitive or grabby, leading to jerky or rough stops. Many say the issues appear soon after ownership and make driving unpleasant.

signals.title: Feels much roomier inside
signals.summary: Customers say the cabin feels very roomy and noticeably more spacious than their previous BMWs. Many highlight roomy rear seats with good legroom, making tall passengers, children, and pets more comfortable in the back.

signals.title: Enjoy the various drive modes
signals.summary: Customers enjoy the range of driving modes and like experimenting with My Modes. They call out Sport mode for a sporty feel, Personal mode for customization like lighting and HUD, and Comfort/Efficient modes for a smooth daily ride and better battery use.

signals.title: Only the driver door unlocks
signals.summary: The car often only unlocks the driver door when approaching or using the key, leaving rear doors locked or failing to open. Customers find this behavior confusing, hard to change because the setting is not obvious, and sometimes the auto-lock can act unexpectedly.

signals.title: Apple CarPlay is glitchy and unreliable
signals.summary: Customers report CarPlay is unreliable and difficult to use, with problems pairing or connecting and media or audio not showing or playing correctly. Some drivers find the interface hard to operate and have disconnected it because of these issues.

signals.title: Hard to find compatible charging stations
signals.summary: Customers say it is difficult to locate available and compatible public chargers near them. They report stations are often scarce, out of service or occupied, placed in inconvenient or unsafe locations, and Electrify America coverage feels insufficient in their area.

signals.title: Can't find odometer in dash
signals.summary: I can't find the odometer or trip mileage in the instrument cluster and the controls to access it are confusing and unintuitive. Many customers needed help or dealer assistance to locate the mileage display.

signals.title: Stays planted and very responsive
signals.summary: Drivers say the car feels planted and very responsive. They enjoy the smooth, comfortable ride and sporty, confident handling that makes driving a joy.

signals.title: Too many menus and the screen gets dirty
signals.summary: The touchscreen feels cluttered and hard to navigate, with too many icons and submenus that make it difficult to find controls. It also smudges easily, attracts dust, can be hard to see in bright light, and sometimes responds slowly.

signals.title: Really love the highway assistant
signals.summary: Customers say the highway assistant makes highway driving and long commutes easier and more relaxing. They appreciate the hands-free and automated driving features as reliable, convenient, and a key reason they value the car.

signals.title: Can't permanently turn off auto start stop
signals.summary: The engine shuts off at every stop and many customers find it irritating and inconvenient. There is no obvious off button, so drivers have to dig through menus or use sport mode each time, and some report the restart feels harsh and jolting.

signals.title: Really happy with the infotainment interface and usability
signals.summary: Customers say the infotainment interface is enjoyable, intuitive, and responsive. They appreciate the clear layout, customizable shortcuts, and balance between digital and physical controls, and some mentioned it was straightforward to learn and use.

signals.title: Charging is too slow and inconsistent
signals.summary: Customers report that charging is too slow and does not always reach expected speeds. They also experience inconsistent scheduled charging and find guidance about recommended charge limits unclear when they need extra range.

signals.title: Too many menus and touchscreens
signals.summary: Customers say the shift to touchscreen controls and lots of menus makes the system hard to use and distracting while driving. They find the interface clunky and unintuitive, requiring many taps and a noticeable learning curve to access basic functions. Study: Menu structure of infotainment system: 13 % dissatisfied, 36 % top-2 (US study 2025).

signals.title: Wireless charger barely charges and won't fit phones
signals.summary: Customers say the in-car wireless charging pad often charges slowly or inconsistently and sometimes does not charge at all. They also say the pad is poorly sized or positioned so phones do not fit or sit flat, requiring wiggling or a cable, and some report buzzing, a nonworking passenger pad, or the tray turning itself back on. Study: Phone charging: 10 % dissatisfied, 56 % top-2 (US study 2025).

signals.title: Hidden vents are hard to find and adjust
signals.summary: Customers say the air vents and controls are hidden, hard to find, and difficult to aim. The touchscreen-only layout and lack of physical knobs make adjusting fan and temperature slow, confusing, and distracting while driving. Study: Operation of heater/ AC controls: 15 % dissatisfied, 29 % top-2 (US study 2025).
